supersedes.reason: R1's single licensed rehearsal returned a fail-closed NO_VERDICT before either engine (python3 -I omitted the script directory from sys.path, so runner_r1's bare sibling import raised ModuleNotFoundError). R2 repaired that and the R1 review's D1-D13, and its hostile source review found the new authorization-lease custody path jointly unsatisfiable: the service user cannot create a lease inside a directory that the same check requires to be root-owned and not group/world writable. R3 repaired the privilege boundary, and its hostile source review confirmed that repair and the unchanged mathematics but found the coordinator choreography jointly unsatisfiable in the same never-executed-integration class: the sealed authorization template ordered an external root mint, then a service-user dry run, then a unit start, while the unit's own ExecStartPre=+ mints again, so an honest launch on a correctly configured host would have died MINT_ALREADY_SPENT before the supervisor. R4 repairs the deployment choreography only: one atomic systemd path, mint -> service-identity dry run -> supervisor -> retire, with no external mint. No earlier packet is patched; their authorizations and leases are retired.
supersedes.r2_blocking_finding: REPAIR-1: claim_authorization_lease required a root-owned, non-group/world-writable run parent and then created the lease in it, while the unit runs as User=jc2k0 with an empty capability set. Jointly unsatisfiable; every rehearsal would have failed closed before any mathematics, either at CUSTODY_FAULT PATH_OWNER or on an uncaught PermissionError.
supersedes.r3_blocking_finding: REPAIR-1: authorization_template_r3.json's sealed DEPLOYMENT ORDER said root mint (step c), ops dry run (step d), 'only then start the unit' (step e), while systemd_unit_template_r3.service repeats the mint as its only ExecStartPre=+. mint_claim_r3.sh spends <sealed parent>/spent/<digest>.spent with O_EXCL before anything else exists, so the unit's mint dies MINT_ALREADY_SPENT rc 75 and ExecStart never runs. The review also found that the packet's 'consumes nothing' / 'a failed precondition never consumes this record' wording is true of the lease and false of the mint, which spends first.

charged_theorem.scope_note: the promoted paper theorem is fixed and is not broadened here; this packet is certificate engineering plus mathematical gate repair, and it re-proves nothing that the reviewed theorem report already establishes

K0_UNCONDITIONAL_THEOREM.statement: K0 is a number field of degree exactly 432, Galois and non-abelian over Q; B = Q(zeta42,r3,h) = Q(zeta_168) of degree 48; [3+r3] and [3-r4] are independent in B*/(B*)^3, spanning (Z/3)^2; K0 has exactly one factor and only the idempotents 0 and 1; K0 is finite etale of rank 432 over Z[1/42]; the ramified rational primes are exactly {2,3,7} and 5 is unramified; both registered frames are degree-1 primes, both primes split completely with exactly 432 frames, and the registered p^2 frame is the unique Hensel lift.
K0_UNCONDITIONAL_THEOREM.census: layer-restricted: only L0-L4 non-corroboration gates feed this boolean
independent_of: any degree-432 or degree-144 irreducibility claim

E_CONDITIONAL_RATIO_THEOREM.statement: given the literal displayed E = (9+5*r3)*A1*W1^4 + (9-5*r3)*A2*W2^4 read out of the sealed E5/E6 bridge, the ratio W1/W2 is K0-rational: q0 = u*(1+i)*(r3-1)/2 with u = A2/A1 and i = r3*(1+2*zeta42^14)/3 satisfies E by direct substitution, and the four branches q0*i^k are four distinct elements of K0, so t^4-c splits completely over K0 and no field extension is needed.
E_CONDITIONAL_RATIO_THEOREM.engine_note: single-engine stdlib Python. k0_field_cert_r4.gp carries no cube-root layer and cannot substitute q0 into E; its L5 block reads the literal E data and certifies the base-level reduction chain only. That is corroboration and the terminal says so; the R1 terminal's E_CONDITIONAL flag was an overstatement (review defect D7).
E_CONDITIONAL_RATIO_THEOREM.census: layer-restricted: only L5 non-corroboration gates feed this boolean
E_CONDITIONAL_RATIO_THEOREM.if_E_is_corrected: this layer must be recomputed; the unconditional layer is untouched

aws_route.instance_type_pin_status: EXACT. R1 shipped a six-member allowlist because the type behind the label r6b was unknown; the R1 rehearsal ran on r6i.large, so R2 pins that single type. Any other type is a source change and a new R-number.
aws_route.gp_binary_pin: coordinator-supplied path and SHA-256, verified by runner_r4 against the on-disk binary; execution_pins_r4.json additionally records the binary hash observed on the R1 rehearsal host for reporting only
aws_route.artifact_mode: 0444 after fsync; created with O_CREAT|O_EXCL on the final name, never overwritten and never staged through a temporary sidecar
aws_route.launch_lease: two independent one-shot gates on opposite sides of the privilege boundary, both before any try block: root mints at most one claim per authorization digest, once, inside the unit (spent/<digest>.spent, O_EXCL, created first, by mint_claim_r4.sh), and the unprivileged supervisor takes at most one consumption lease inside the service-owned run directory (.jc2-k0-r4-authorization-<digest>.lease, O_CREAT|O_EXCL, taken last, after every precondition). A used authorization can never be presented again; a failed precondition never consumes one.
aws_route.local_execution_mode: none; absent a live IMDSv2 identity the supervisor exits without running any mathematics
aws_route.isolated_interpreter: python3 -I -B is retained and is now a checked property: runner_r4 refuses to run outside isolated mode and loads its sealed siblings by manifest-verified path, never through sys.path

privilege_boundary.sealed_parent: root:root, mode without group or world write, symlink-free, no writable ancestor; verified unprivileged by require_root_owned_immutable and again by mint_claim_r4.sh as root with a realpath test. The service never writes here.
privilege_boundary.run_directory: root-minted, chowned to jc2k0, mode exactly 0700; the only path in ReadWritePaths. The supervisor creates no directory.
privilege_boundary.claim_token: <run dir>/.jc2-k0-r4-claim-<digest>.json, root:root 0444, minted by root inside the service-owned directory. The service cannot create it (no chown to root) and cannot modify it (no write bit for anyone but root; empty CapabilityBoundingSet excludes CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE and CAP_CHOWN). Deleting it denies only itself: CLAIM_ABSENT, nothing consumed.
privilege_boundary.mint: the unit's FIRST ExecStartPre=+ mint_claim_r4.sh, root, one-shot via spent/<digest>.spent created with O_EXCL before anything else exists. It is the only mint: a coordinator never runs it by hand, because a hand mint makes the unit's own ExecStartPre die MINT_ALREADY_SPENT. R4 takes the absolute run directory as one argument and derives the parent and the run name from it, so the unit uses a single <ABSOLUTE_RUN_DIRECTORY> sentinel in the mint, the dry run, ReadWritePaths and the retirement.
privilege_boundary.retire: ExecStopPost=+ retire_claim_r4.sh, root, seals the finished run directory to root-owned read-only.
privilege_boundary.on_host_dry_run: the unit's SECOND ExecStartPre, with no + prefix, so systemd runs it as User=jc2k0 in the unit's own sandbox and mount namespace, after the mint and before ExecStart. custody_selftest_r4.py --on-host-dry-run calls the supervisor's own verify_custody_preconditions and stops there: it creates, writes and removes nothing, and its call graph never reaches claim_authorization_lease, so it cannot consume the one-shot claim. A non-zero exit (rc 70) aborts the start before ExecStart. It is not free: the mint has already spent the digest, so a refusal here retires the coordinator record exactly as a supervisor refusal does.
privilege_boundary.fault_discipline: every custody filesystem call converts OSError into a CustodyFault; main converts anything else into CUSTODY_FAULT UNCLASSIFIED with rc 70. No custody path can produce a traceback.
privilege_boundary.pre_mint_advisory: optional, outside the unit, and the only check that costs nothing: custody_selftest_r4.py --pre-mint-advisory verifies the sealed parent, the frozen record and the service identity and REQUIRES that nothing has been minted yet (the run directory must not exist and the spent marker must be absent), so it refuses PREMINT_ALREADY_MINTED the moment the unit has started and can never be run in place of the unit's dry run.

ordered_unit_sequence: ExecStartPre=+ mint_claim_r4.sh <run dir> <auth json> jc2k0   (root, one-shot)
ExecStartPre= <python> -I -B custody_selftest_r4.py --on-host-dry-run --run-path <run dir> --authorization <auth json> --out -   (jc2k0, unit sandbox, no lease)
ExecStart= aws_worker_r4.sh ... aws_supervisor_r4.py --authorization <auth json>   (jc2k0, verify then lease)
ExecStopPost=+ retire_claim_r4.sh <run dir>   (root, seals evidence, runs even if the start aborted)

repairs.REPAIR-1: the deployment choreography: one atomic systemd path. The unit's first ExecStartPre=+ mints as root; its second ExecStartPre, with no prefix, runs custody_selftest_r4.py --on-host-dry-run as User=jc2k0 in the unit's own sandbox against that token and takes no lease; ExecStart runs the supervisor, which verifies and only then burns; ExecStopPost=+ retires as root. The authorization template, the unit, this preregistration, the README and the review request describe exactly that path, and there is no external mint.
repairs.REPAIR-1c: mint_claim_r4.sh takes the absolute run directory as a single argument and derives the sealed parent and the run name from it, so the unit uses one <ABSOLUTE_RUN_DIRECTORY> sentinel in all four places and the mint/dry-run/ReadWritePaths/retire agreement is mechanically checkable. Every gate of the script is unchanged; R3's four-argument call is now a usage refusal.
repairs.REPAIR-1d: the cost wording: 'consumes nothing' and 'a failed precondition never consumes this record' are true of the lease and false of the mint. Every sealed file now says that the mint has already spent the digest, and custody_selftest_r4.wording_controls freezes that.
repairs.carried_from_R3: the privilege boundary itself (sealed parent, root-minted service-owned run directory, root-owned 0444 claim token, verify-then-burn lease, OSError-to-CustodyFault discipline), the runner run-directory law, and the GP CRT and charframes edits are carried unchanged from R3 and are not re-opened.
